assumptions: Host-directed correction of the Periastra Meridian archive, renamed Periastra Zenith because a --no-publish correction cannot overwrite a toys/ slug that already holds different bytes. The corrected archive is toys/mara-masque-periastra-zenith.

Exactly one thing changes: the telescope and the way the dome carries it. Everything else in the object stays where it is. Within that one change, the two free variables the brief grants - where the axis meets the floor, and the tube's length - are set at y +13.0 and 85.3 mm after the first independent review read the silhouette as a gun barrel.

FOUR of the five print designs are frozen byte for byte - base, inlay, sun counter and moon counter - and measure/check_fit.py asserts all four published sha256 on every run and fails the build if any of them moves.

Every constant the brief listed keeps its value: BASE 190.0, HEIGHT 24.0, WALL 3.0, OPENING 184.0, FLOOR 11.0, CELL 22.0, ROWS 8, BOARD 176.0, POCKET_DEPTH, INLAY_SIZE, INLAY_THICK, INLAY_CHAMFER, LEDGE_TOP 21.0, LEDGE_DEPTH 3.0, LEDGE_LENGTH 24.0, SILL_TOP 17.0, PIER_INNER 88.0, ROOF_CLEARANCE 0.8, ROOF_SIZE 182.4, PLATE 3.0, ROOF_CORNER 1.2, CORNER 2.0, LIFT 100.0, COUNTER_DIAMETER 20.0, COUNTER_HEIGHT 7.0, COUNTER_CHAMFER 1.0, DRUM_RADIUS 75.0, DRUM_HEIGHT 11.7, DOME_SPHERE_RADIUS 75.0, DOME_RISE 75.0, the rotation-ring groove and its relief, SLIT_WIDTH 30.0, SLIT_FAR_RUN 30.0, TUBE_RADIUS 7.5, TUBE_BORE_RADIUS 3.5, TUBE_BORE_DEPTH 13.0. The dome stays an exact hemisphere on a visible drum and the plate stays bare.

The slit still runs the full height of the dome. Only its lower limit moves, from z 3.0 at the plate top to z 14.7 at the drum top, so the slit cuts the dome alone and the drum's rotation ring is continuous all the way round.

The telescope is its own pier. The dome is a solid hemisphere and the slit removes every piece of material inside it, so the floor of the slit is the one thing the tube can reach without a bracket. The fork, the two arms, the keel and the rectangular foot block are deleted.

Five characteristics are scoped out by the host and carried forward as disclosures rather than repaired: the open 4.0 mm perimeter reveal, the gravity-seated inlays, the Sun mark reading as a cog, the two orientation marks sitting one cell off the board centreline, and the dome being a solid hemisphere.

build_plan.exit_criteria: part_base.step, part_inlay.step, part_sun_counter.step and part_moon_counter.step reproduce their published sha256 byte for byte and part_roof.step does not; each of the five designs passes its own isolated build, wall and visual round before the combined entry is reviewed; and measure/check_fit.py proves on the BUILT part_roof.step that the roof is one connected solid with no floating lumps, that exactly one lump of material stands inside the slit at six heights from z15.2 to z78.0 and is centred on x = 0 within 0.01 mm, that the roof carries exactly one planar face in the floor plane with the foot as a hole in it and no coincident face anywhere, that the tube reaches the floor at z14.7 on a foot of at least 15.0 x 19.58 mm fused to it, that the drum ring is a single unbroken band at six heights from z4.0 to z14.0 with no gap anywhere, that 0.0 mm3 of roof lies outboard of the 75.0 mm drum radius below the springing line, that the roof is mirror-symmetric about x = 0 under 1 mm3, that the muzzle stands between 2.5 mm and 7.0 mm proud of the 75.0 mm sphere, and that the muzzle stays under the apex; all 58 occurrences export as named single solids; and one independent critic reads the canonical images - including a straight side elevation with the camera level with the dome, three-quarter views into the open slit, the drum photographed from four azimuths, the plan view down the slit and the whole board at playing scale - and answers the silhouette, support, ring-continuity and unfinished-surface questions before learning what the object is.

components.duty: Carry all 24 counters and support the removable roof.
components.form: 190 by 190 by 24 mm rounded square solid-bottom plinth; 3 mm perimeter walls drop to z17 along the open side spans, retaining z24 corner piers. 176 mm 8x8 board on a floor at z11, 22 mm cells. The 32 cells where file + rank is even carry a BLIND pocket 22.0 mm across and 2.0 mm deep with all four plan corners chamfered 1.0 mm, on 9.0 mm of continuous backing - the house tiled-board fit layer, scaled to this 22 mm square. The old 0.8 mm recess with its 0.3 mm sloped lip and 1.5 mm rounded corners is gone. Two 3 mm half-disc orientation marks on the mid-file edges, unchanged and untouched.
components.interfaces: 184 mm square inner opening; four integral 3 by 3 mm corner ledges from floor z11 to top z21 seat the roof plate with 0.8 mm lateral clearance per side. Each of the 32 pockets takes one inlay with 0.25 mm of clearance per side; the inlay top finishes flush with the board floor at z11.
components.name: Observatory board base
components.placement: Centred on x=y=0; bottom z=0; floor z=11; board spans -88 to 88 on x and y.

components.duty: Close and store the populated board, and read unmistakably as a working observatory - an instrument standing on its own footing inside an open dome - when it is lifted clear.
components.form: 182.4 mm square backing plate 3.0 mm thick with 1.2 mm corners, flat underside, no notches, cut-outs or holes. A visible 150 mm drum of radius 75.0 and height 11.7 stands on it, carrying one rotation-ring seam 2.0 mm along the axis by 1.0 mm deep, centred 4.0 mm below the drum top, its upper wall relieved at 50 degrees. That ring is CONTINUOUS: nothing is cut through the drum wall at any point on its circumference, and no material of the roof lies outside the 75.0 mm drum radius at any height between the plate top and the drum top. An EXACT HEMISPHERE of radius 75.0, centred on the axis at the drum top z14.7, rises from there: base radius 75.0, rise 75.0, so at its base the dome surface is vertical and flows continuously into the drum wall. One 30.0 mm shutter slit with parallel square-cut walls is cut on a single meridian in the YZ plane through the DOME ONLY: it runs from 30.0 mm of surface arc (22.9 degrees) down the far side, over the apex, and down the near flank to the springing line at z14.7, where it stops. Its floor is the exposed drum top, a level rectangle 30.0 mm wide bounded in y by the drum's own circle. A telescope STANDS ON THAT FLOOR: a 15.0 mm outer tube 85.3 mm long measured along its axis from the floor plane, inclined 50.0 degrees above horizontal, its axis on x = 0 meeting the floor at y = +13.0, with an open 7.0 mm muzzle bore 13.0 mm deep leaving a 4.0 mm tube wall. The floor plane itself cuts the tube off flat on a level 15.0 x 19.58 mm elliptical foot fused to the drum, and the root is blended into the floor with a 6.0 mm cove fillet carried right round that foot, measured on the built STEP at 26.425 mm across the slit and 35.246 mm along it, 1.788 mm clear of each slit wall and 3.618 mm clear of the far wall. Nothing else stands in the slit at any height: no fork, no arms, no keel, no pier and no foot block. The tube leaves the dome 32.4 degrees from the apex and its muzzle stands 3.899 mm proud of the 75.0 mm sphere, 0.26 of its own diameter, with its top at z84.86 local. The whole roof is ONE connected solid and measures mirror-symmetric about x = 0 at 0.0000 mm3. The flat plate margin round the dome is 16.2 mm and is bare: no railing, walkway, ladder, panelling, ribs, rivets, windows, finial or decoration of any kind.
components.interfaces: Flat plate underside rests on the four base ledges at z21. No skirt, hinge, latch, magnet or hardware of any kind, and no assembly step. Lifts straight up 100 mm to reveal the board.
components.name: Observatory dome roof
components.placement: Seated: plate underside at z21, drum z24 to z35.7, slit floor and dome springing line z35.7, nominal dome apex z110.7, built high point z109.185 at the slit shoulders because the slit runs over the apex, telescope foot centred at y = +13.0 on the slit floor and its muzzle top at z105.86.

concept.interaction: Lift the roof 100 mm straight up and set it aside. Play English draughts unchanged: men move and capture diagonally forward one square, capture is compulsory, a man reaching the far row is crowned and its turn ends there, a king moves and captures one square diagonally in all four directions. Roof flat backing plate down with the dome apex up, so the hemisphere is self-supporting from its vertical base and the telescope, inclined 50 degrees above horizontal, presents a 40-degree slope from vertical at its steepest downward-facing surface and clears the 45-degree gate by 5 degrees with nothing under its length. Counters flat on either face - the two faces are identical, so the choice is free; the bed contact is the 2.0 mm rim band plus the coplanar flat top of the raised symbol.
risks: The telescope is a cantilever taken entirely at its root: 85.3 mm of tube overhung from a 15.0 x 19.58 mm elliptical foot, 65.3 mm above the floor with 54.8 mm of horizontal run and its centre of mass 17.8 mm outside the foot horizontally. In FDM the layer lines at that root run across the bending plane. The root is blended into the floor with a 6.0 mm cove fillet carried right round the foot, measured on the built STEP at 26.425 mm across the slit and 35.246 mm along it. NO PHYSICAL TEST BACKS THAT FILLET. It is a geometric mitigation only.

check_overhang still fails both counters on its connected-region span proxy: the field floor is one connected ring, so the proxy reports the full 14.0 mm field diameter against a 12 mm allowance. Because two print entries fail a print gate, the assembled-object make_round was run without --require-component-passes. The diagonal material bridge between two chamfered pockets measures 1.414 mm, below the 3 mm minimum feature width the rest of this set observes. Inherited unchanged from the frozen base and disclosed rather than engineered away.

The 32 inlays are loose and the closed box has an open 4.0 mm perimeter reveal. An inlay is 2.0 mm thick and can leave through it; a counter is 7.0 mm thick and cannot. The host scoped both out, so they are recorded as disclosed limitations and neither is attempted.

The frozen Wish for the published set says "English draughts between two comet streams". An earlier correction removed the comets in favour of the Sun and the Moon and this revision continues that. concept.signature_decision: A 150 mm hemispherical observatory dome whose shutter runs from the observatory floor over the apex and down the far flank, with a long telescope standing on its own footing on that floor and lying diagonally across the open dome, most of its length visible down the slit and only its mouth clearing the shell. The dome is the lid; lifting it reveals a populated draughts board whose dark squares are inlaid tiles in a second colour. This revision moves the instrument from a barrel poking through a wall to an instrument standing in a room, and it repairs the rotation ring the old mount broke. The footing sits at the low end of the brief's y window and the tube at the low end of its length window, so the tube leaves the shell as radially as the brief allows and stands as little of itself in the open as the brief allows.
concept.summary: English draughts under an observatory dome: the Sun side and the Moon side meet across an inlaid chequerboard, and the dome that watches them - shutter open from floor to apex, with a long telescope standing on the floor inside it - is the lid of the box.

design_changes.change: The shutter slit's lower limit moves from z 3.0 to z 14.7, the drum top, which is also the dome's springing line and the sphere's centre height. design_changes.change: The telescope stands on the slit floor as its own pier: 85.3 mm long on an axis 50.0 degrees above horizontal meeting the floor at (0.0, +13.0, 14.7), cut off flat by the floor plane on a level 15.0 x 19.58 mm elliptical foot fused to the drum. Measured on the built STEP it leaves the dome 32.37 degrees from the apex; its muzzle stands 2.586 mm proud of the 75.0 mm sphere measured on the axis and 3.899 mm measured to the farthest material on the muzzle rim, which is 0.26 of a tube diameter.

design_changes.reason: Host correction, with the host's own numbers. Raising the elevation alone does not fix it: 35 degrees exits at 55.0 degrees, 50 at 48.5 and 65 at 41.6, because a ray that starts 35 mm off the axis and low leaves low. THE PIVOT IS THE LEVER, NOT THE ANGLE. Moving the pivot to the floor on the slit's mid-plane is what buys the 32.4-degree exit. 50 degrees is a hard floor for the elevation: the steepest downward-facing surface of a cylinder inclined E degrees above horizontal has its normal E degrees from vertical, so at the shipped 35 degrees the tube was a 35-degree overhang and needed the keel. check_overhang passes part_roof at a 0.4 mm nozzle with the keel deleted. The foot at y +13.0 and the length of 85.3 mm are the low ends of the brief's two free windows, taken after the first independent review read the silhouette as a gun: y +13.0 puts the axis nearer the sphere's own centre so the tube leaves more radially, and 85.3 mm is the shortest length that keeps BOTH readings of the brief's 2.5-7.0 mm projection window - its own axis figure and the built material figure - inside it.
